speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have chronic pain in your left shoulder without any history of trauma. To help me narrow down the cause, how many years has this pain been persisting, and does it worsen at night or with specific movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the pain disrupting your sleep and limiting daily activities like brushing your hair suggests significant inflammation or structural damage. Given your age and 2-month history, could you describe exactly what happens when you try to lift your arm above your head or reach behind your back? Also, do you notice any visible swelling or warmth in the left shoulder area?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mention of diabetes is clinically relevant as it can predispose you to specific shoulder conditions. When I perform a physical exam and ask you to lift your arm to 90 degrees, does the pain stop you from moving it fully (pseudoparalysis), or can you still move it but with severe pain?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Calcific Tendonitis of the Rotator Cuff
